projects.name: Customer Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
Analytics dashboard platform with three core capability areas:

1. CUSTOMER CSV DATA PROCESSING — ingest, validate, clean, and model customer CSV exports (schema drift, encoding, deduplication, PII handling) into a queryable analytics store.

2. APPLICATION LOG ANALYSIS — collect, parse, and aggregate application logs into operational and behavioral metrics (error rates, latency percentiles, request volumes, funnel events).

3. VISUALIZATION COMPONENTS — a reusable chart/component library plus the dashboard surfaces presenting both data domains, with filtering, drill-down, and export.

Structure: four milestones (Platform Foundation, Customer Data Pipeline, Log Analysis Pipeline, Visualization & Delivery), each decomposed into tasks sized for execution in 1-3 days at complexity <= 6, with explicit cross-cutting dependencies so work can be parallelized across a small team.

Out of scope for v1: real-time streaming ingestion, ML forecasting, mobile clients.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-engineering, visualization, logs

tasks.name: M1 — Platform Foundation
tasks.details:
Milestone M1. Establish the shared technical substrate both data pipelines and the visualization layer depend on: repository/tooling, environment + CI, analytics warehouse and schemas, data contracts, and security/PII policy.

Exit criteria:
- Repo, linting, test harness, and CI pipeline run green on an empty app.
- Warehouse provisioned (dev + staging) with connection handling and migration tooling.
- Shared data contracts for customer and log datasets documented and agreed with stakeholders.
- PII classification and retention policy signed off by security.

Blocks M2 and M3. Should complete first; downstream milestones can start on contract-dependent tasks once data contracts land.

tasks.name: M2 — Customer CSV Data Pipeline
tasks.details:
Milestone M2. Turn raw customer CSV exports into clean, deduplicated, queryable customer analytics tables.

Scope: file intake, schema detection and drift handling, type coercion/encoding, validation and quarantine of bad rows, PII masking, deduplication and identity resolution, incremental load strategy, and a curated customer dimension/fact model with quality monitoring.

Exit criteria:
- A customer CSV file can be dropped in and land as validated rows in the warehouse with a run report.
- >99% of valid rows pass validation; rejected rows are quarantined with reasons.
- PII fields masked/tokenized per M1 policy.
- Dedup and incremental (re)loads are idempotent and covered by tests.

Depends on M1 data contracts and warehouse.

tasks.name: M3 — Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details:
Milestone M3. Convert raw application logs into metrics and events the dashboard can chart.

Scope: log shipping/collection, format parsing (structured + legacy unstructured), normalization to a canonical event schema, enrichment (service, environment, geo/UA as available), aggregation into pre-computed metrics (error rate, latency p50/p95/p99, request volume, funnel events), retention/rollup tiers, and backfill capability.

Exit criteria:
- Logs from all production services flow into the canonical event table with parse-success rate reported.
- Core metrics available at 1-minute (recent) and 1-hour (historical) granularity.
- Backfill of a 7-day window reproduces the same numbers as live ingestion.
- Alerting threshold queries documented.

Depends on M1 data contracts and warehouse.

tasks.name: M4 — Visualization & Dashboard Delivery
tasks.details:
Milestone M4. Build the reusable visualization component library and assemble the two dashboard surfaces (customer analytics, application health), then harden and launch.

Scope: design tokens + chart component library, query/semantic layer between frontend and warehouse, dashboard shell with global filters and drill-down, the customer and log dashboard pages, export/share, performance budgets, accessibility, and a beta launch with rollout plan.

Exit criteria:
- Component library published with docs and visual regression coverage.
- Both dashboard pages live behind auth for a pilot group of users.
- p95 dashboard load < 2.5s on the defined performance budget.
- Accessibility audit passes (WCAG 2.1 AA on core flows).

Depends on M2 and M3 for real data; UI shell and component library can start after M1.

tasks.name: 1.1 Repo & toolchain scaffolding
tasks.details:
Initialize the monorepo and baseline developer experience so all later work lands on a consistent footing.

Deliverables:
- Repo structure (apps/ for dashboard + API, packages/ for shared libs, pipelines/ for data jobs).
- Language/toolchain pinned (runtime version file, dependency lockfile).
- Linters and formatters configured with pre-commit hooks.
- Test runner wired for one unit-test example per package.

Done when: a fresh clone passes lint + tests with a single documented command.

tasks.name: 1.2 CI pipeline & staging deploy
tasks.details:
Stand up continuous integration and a repeatable path to deploy.

Deliverables:
- CI workflow: install → lint → typecheck → unit test → build, on PR and main.
- PR checks enforced (required status, branch protection).
- Staging deploy job (manual trigger acceptable for v1).
- Build artifact/caching so CI finishes under 8 minutes.

Done when: a trivial PR runs green end-to-end without manual steps.

tasks.name: 1.3 Warehouse provisioning & migration tooling
tasks.details:
Provision the analytics warehouse and the migration workflow that all pipelines write through.

Deliverables:
- Dev and staging warehouse instances (or schemas) provisioned via IaC, not clicked.
- Connection pooling + credential handling via the secrets store (see 1.6).
- Migration tool selected and configured; empty baseline migration applied in both envs.
- Separate schemas for raw / staged / curated layers.

Done when: `migrate up` on a clean environment produces the full baseline schema, twice without error (idempotent).

tasks.name: 1.4 Data contracts for customer & log datasets
tasks.details:
Write down the shared definitions the CSV pipeline, log pipeline, and dashboard all code against — this is the single highest-leverage unblocker in M1.

Deliverables:
- Customer dataset contract: column names, types, nullability, allowed values/enums, required keys, example rows, known historical variants.
- Log event contract: canonical field list (timestamp, service, env, level, request id, trace id, status, latency_ms, message, attributes map), plus source-format mapping table.
- Sample fixture files for each contract checked into the repo.
- Contract-review sign-off from the dashboard and pipeline owners.

Done when: both contracts are documented in one place and M2/M3 owners confirm they can build against them.

tasks.name: 1.5 PII classification, masking & retention policy
tasks.details:
Decide and document what counts as PII in customer and log data, how it is protected in motion and at rest, and how long it lives.

Deliverables:
- Field-level PII classification table for the customer dataset (direct identifiers, quasi-identifiers, sensitive attributes).
- Masking/tokenization approach: hashing + salt keys, format-preserving masking, or column encryption — pick one per field class and justify.
- Access-control model: who can query unmasked data.
- Retention schedule per table, including log retention and rollup expiry.
- Security sign-off recorded.

Done when: policy is published and both pipeline tasks 2.5 and 3.x can implement against it without further decisions.

tasks.name: 1.6 Secrets & environment configuration
tasks.details:
Make configuration and secrets handling consistent across local, dev, staging, and prod so pipelines don't hardcode credentials.

Deliverables:
- Secrets manager (or platform equivalent) wired for warehouse creds, storage keys, hashing salts.
- Env var convention + .env.example; nothing secret in git.
- Config loader shared by pipelines and API with fail-fast validation on missing keys.
- Documented local bootstrap in the README.

Done when: a new developer can run the stack locally following only the README, with zero shared passwords.

tasks.name: 2.1 CSV intake, file registry & run tracking
tasks.details:
Build the entry point: how a CSV file physically arrives, is registered, and is tracked.

Deliverables:
- Landing zone (object storage prefix or ingest folder) with a documented drop convention.
- File registry table: filename, content hash, size, row count, arrival time, source system, status.
- Idempotency: re-uploading the same file by content hash is detected and skipped, not re-processed.
- Trigger: scheduled poll or upload event that enqueues a processing run and records a run id.

Done when: two identical files produce exactly one processing run and the second is recorded as an intentional skip.

Depends on 1.3 (warehouse) and 1.6 (secrets).

tasks.name: 2.2 Schema detection & drift handling
tasks.details:
Detect the shape of each incoming file and flag anything that deviates from the agreed contract.

Deliverables:
- Header + delimiter + encoding detection (UTF-8, UTF-8-BOM, Latin-1) with test fixtures for each.
- Column mapping from source headers to canonical names (handles renamed/reordered/extra/missing columns).
- Drift report per run: new columns, dropped columns, type changes, unexpected nulls.
- Configurable drift policy: tolerate-and-flag vs. hard-fail per column class.

Done when: a fixture set covering clean, reordered, renamed, extra-column, and missing-column files each produce the correct drift classification rather than an outright crash.

Depends on 1.4 data contracts.

tasks.name: 2.3 Type coercion & encoding normalization
tasks.details:
Convert every field into a trustworthy typed value.

Deliverables:
- Type coercion for dates (multiple formats + timezone assumption documented), numbers (thousands separators, currency symbols, parenthesised negatives), and booleans (Y/N/yes/1/true).
- Trim/whitespace and full-width character normalization; quoted-field and embedded-newline handling verified.
- Explicit null-vs-empty-vs-placeholder handling (NA, N/A, null, -, "").
- Unit tests per coercion rule, including the nasty cases above.

Done when: a fixture file of malformed values produces predictable typed output or an explicit rejection reason — never a silent wrong value.

tasks.name: 2.4 Row validation & quarantine
tasks.details:
Decide per row whether it is trustworthy enough to use, and preserve the failures instead of discarding them.

Deliverables:
- Declarative rule set (required fields, enum membership, range checks, referential/cross-field checks, email/phone format).
- Quarantine table storing rejected rows verbatim plus rule id, field, reason, run id, file name, row number.
- Per-run validation summary: rows in, valid, rejected, rejection rate by rule.
- Threshold enforcement: the run fails loudly if rejection rate exceeds a configured ceiling (protects the curated tables).

Done when: every rejection is traceable back to the exact source file and line, and a deliberately corrupt file cannot corrupt curated tables.

tasks.name: 2.5 PII masking & tokenization in pipeline
tasks.details:
Implement the masking decisions from 1.5 so raw identifiers never reach the curated layer.

Deliverables:
- Deterministic tokenization of direct identifiers (stable salted hash, salt from secrets store, never in code).
- Masking of free-text fields that may contain emails/phones (regex sweep + tests).
- Raw identifiable columns confined to a restricted schema; curated layer exposes only tokens.
- Re-tokenization/rotation runbook (what breaks and how to handle a salt rotation).

Done when: a query against the curated schema returns no raw emails, names, phone numbers, or addresses, and token stability is proven by re-running the same input.

tasks.name: 2.6 Deduplication & identity resolution
tasks.details:
Collapse duplicate customer records — the same human appearing multiple times — without merging distinct people.

Deliverables:
- Match-key strategy: exact keys (email hash, normalized phone, external id) then fuzzy keys (name + address similarity) with a documented threshold.
- Deterministic survivor selection rule (e.g. most recent authoritative source wins).
- Merge log linking survivor record to absorbed source records, so merges are auditable and reversible.
- Explicit guard against false positives: same name + same city must NOT auto-merge.

Done when: a fixture set of known duplicates collapses to the expected count and a fixture set of distinct-but-similar customers produces zero merges.

tasks.name: 2.7 Idempotent incremental load & reprocessing
tasks.details:
Load into the warehouse in a way that can be safely re-run.

Deliverables:
- Staging table + merge/upsert pattern (no blind appends to curated tables).
- Change detection via row hash / updated-at, so unchanged rows are untouched.
- Full-reprocess path: ability to rebuild a date range from raw files on demand.
- Reprocessing safety: a failed run leaves curated tables in their pre-run state (transaction or swap-table pattern).

Done when: running the same file three times leaves row counts and values identical, and a killed mid-run process leaves no partial rows.

tasks.name: 2.8 Curated customer dimension & fact model
tasks.details:
Model the curated customer layer the dashboard will actually query.

Deliverables:
- dim_customer (tokenized identity, attributes, segment, geography, acquisition source, lifecycle dates).
- fct_customer_activity (or equivalent) with the measure columns defined in 1.4.
- Transformation jobs as version-controlled SQL/models with tests (unique keys, not-null, accepted values, referential integrity to dim_customer).
- Column-level documentation/descriptions surfaced to dashboard developers.

Done when: model tests pass in CI and a dashboard developer can answer "active customers by segment last 30 days" with one query and no tribal knowledge.

tasks.name: 2.9 Data quality monitoring & run reports
tasks.details:
Make pipeline health visible so failures are caught by the system, not by a confused dashboard user.

Deliverables:
- Persisted run history: rows in/valid/rejected/loaded, duration, drift findings, status.
- Freshness check: alert when the newest customer data exceeds the expected staleness threshold.
- Volume anomaly check: alert when row counts deviate sharply from trailing average.
- Rejection-rate and drift alerts routed to the owning team's channel.

Done when: a deliberately broken file, a stalled feed, and a 50% volume drop each trigger a distinct, correctly-routed alert.

tasks.name: 3.1 Log collection & shipping across services
tasks.details:
Get logs from every application service to a central durable location.

Deliverables:
- Inventory of services and their current log outputs (stdout, file, vendor agent, syslog).
- Collection agent or platform shipper configured per service, with buffering + retry on destination outage.
- Transport to the analytics landing area, partitioned by date and service.
- Volume baseline measured (GB/day, events/day) so downstream sizing is grounded.

Done when: every service in the inventory has logs arriving in the landing area, and a 15-minute outage of the destination loses no events (buffer replay verified).

tasks.name: 3.2 Structured log parsing to canonical schema
tasks.details:
Parse the primary structured (JSON) log format into the canonical event schema from 1.4.

Deliverables:
- Parser mapping source fields to canonical columns (timestamp, service, env, level, request_id, trace_id, status, latency_ms, message, attributes).
- Timestamp parsing with timezone normalization to UTC; clock-skew outliers flagged not dropped.
- Nested/attribute fields preserved into a map/semi-structured column rather than flattened lossily.
- Golden-file tests: real sample lines in, exact expected canonical rows out.

Done when: a 10k-line sample from each structured-emitting service reaches >= 99.5% parse success with a diff-able golden-file test.

Depends on 1.4 log event contract.

tasks.name: 3.3 Legacy/unstructured log parsing & failure capture
tasks.details:
Handle the older/human-readable log lines that don't carry structure.

Deliverables:
- Ordered pattern set (grok/regex) per source format, applied first-match-wins, version controlled.
- Unmatched lines captured into a parse-failure table with source sample, so patterns can be iteratively improved.
- Parse-success rate metric per service, reported per run.
- A triage loop documented: top unmatched patterns → new rule → regression test.

Done when: parse success for legacy sources exceeds the agreed target (recommend 95%) and every unmatched pattern shape is visible in the failure table, not silently dropped.

tasks.name: 3.4 Enrichment: service, route, UA & geo
tasks.details:
Add the dimensions the dashboard needs to slice by.

Deliverables:
- Service and environment normalization from a lookup table (no free-text service names).
- Request/route extraction and normalization (collapse path params to templates, e.g. /orders/{id}).
- User-agent parsing to device class/browser family; country derivation from IP with raw IP dropped or masked per 1.5.
- Enrichment lookup tables cached and versioned.

Done when: the same route hit with different IDs maps to one route template, and IP-derived geography works without retaining the raw IP in the curated layer.

tasks.name: 3.5 Metric aggregation jobs (error rate, latency percentiles, volume)
tasks.details:
Pre-compute the numbers the dashboard charts so queries stay fast.

Deliverables:
- Aggregation jobs producing: error rate (by service/route/level), latency p50/p95/p99, request volume, unique-ish visitor counts where derivable.
- 1-minute buckets for a recent window (e.g. 48h) and 1-hour buckets for long history.
- Correct percentile method chosen and documented (approximate vs exact trade-off); a test proving p95 matches an independent exact calculation within tolerance.
- Scheduled refresh with a documented SLA (e.g. metrics no older than 5 minutes).

Done when: dashboard-critical metrics for a known 24h window match hand-computed values from raw logs, and refresh latency is measured.

This is the most technically involved task in M3 — if it overruns, split 1-minute vs 1-hour aggregation into separate tasks.

tasks.name: 3.6 Funnel & session event extraction
tasks.details:
Derive ordered step-by-step behaviour from logs for the funnel visualization.

Deliverables:
- Step definitions agreed (e.g. page_view → add_to_cart → checkout_start → purchase) as configuration, not hardcoded.
- Session stitching by session_id where present, else by user token + inactivity gap.
- Per-step counts, conversion rates, and drop-off; out-of-order and repeated steps handled by documented rules.
- Validation against a known-good manual count for one day of traffic.

Done when: funnel conversion for a reference day matches the manual count and step definitions can be changed without a code deploy.

tasks.name: 3.7 Partitioning, rollups & retention tiers
tasks.details:
Keep log storage cost bounded without breaking the dashboard's history.

Deliverables:
- Date-based partitioning on the event table with partition pruning verified in query plans.
- Tiering: raw events short-lived, aggregate rollups long-lived, per the 1.5 retention schedule.
- Automated expiry/purge job with a dry-run mode and a logged record of what it deleted.
- Query-cost check: representative dashboard queries stay within a stated scan-size budget.

Done when: dashboard queries over 90 days of history scan only the relevant partitions, and the purge job runs in dry-run without deleting anything unexpected.

tasks.name: 3.8 Backfill tooling & parity validation
tasks.details:
Prove the pipeline can be replayed and that history is trustworthy.

Deliverables:
- Backfill command taking a date range and re-deriving events + aggregates from archived raw logs.
- Parity check: backfilled metrics vs. originally-ingested metrics diffed automatically with a tolerance threshold.
- Documented limits: how far back raw logs are retained and therefore how far backfill can reach.
- Runbook: how to repair a corrupted day without manual SQL surgery.

Done when: a 7-day backfill reproduces original metrics within tolerance with zero manual intervention.

tasks.name: 4.1 Design tokens & component library foundation
tasks.details:
Establish the visual language and package structure before anyone writes a chart.

Deliverables:
- Design tokens: color (including a colorblind-safe categorical palette), spacing, typography, elevation, motion.
- Component package skeleton with Storybook (or equivalent) running locally and in CI.
- Light/dark theming wired from day one.
- Contribution conventions: naming, prop API style, test requirements.

Done when: Storybook builds in CI and a token change propagates to every example component without touching component code.

tasks.name: 4.2 Core chart components (line, bar, sparkline, heatmap)
tasks.details:
Build the time-series and comparison charts both dashboards depend on.

Deliverables:
- Line chart with multiple series, gap handling, and time-bucket-aware axis formatting.
- Bar and stacked-bar charts with grouped/stacked modes.
- Sparkline for KPI tiles; heatmap for hourly/day-of-week density.
- Shared chart API: consistent loading, empty, error, and partial-data states.
- Responsive behavior verified at three breakpoints.

Done when: each component has docs, an empty-state example, and a visual regression baseline.

tasks.name: 4.3 Data table & faceted filter components
tasks.details:
The controls users touch most — get these right early.

Deliverables:
- Data table: server-side sorting and pagination, sticky header, column visibility, numeric formatting.
- Faceted filter components: date-range picker (with presets: 24h/7d/30d/90d/custom), multi-select, searchable dropdown.
- Filter state serialized to URL so a view is shareable and reload-safe.
- Debounced filter application with a visible pending state.

Done when: changing filters updates the URL, a page reload restores the exact same view, and rapid filter changes trigger one query, not five.

tasks.name: 4.4 Query/semantic layer API & caching
tasks.details:
Put a governed API between the UI and raw tables so the frontend never writes SQL.

Deliverables:
- Metric endpoints with explicit contracts: customer metrics, log/health metrics, funnel, dimensions for filters.
- Whitelisted dimensions/measures — no arbitrary SQL from the client; validate and reject unknown fields.
- Response caching with TTL matched to data refresh SLA, plus cache-key design (filters + user scope).
- Pagination and result-size caps; query timeout and graceful degradation to "data unavailable" rather than a hung request.

Done when: every chart in 4.2/4.3 can be fed from this API alone, invalid filter input is rejected with a clear error, and repeated identical requests hit cache.

Depends on 2.8 (customer model) and 3.5 (metrics).

tasks.name: 4.5 Dashboard shell: auth, navigation, global filters
tasks.details:
The frame every dashboard page lives inside.

Deliverables:
- Auth integration (SSO or existing provider), protected routes, session handling, and a signed-out state.
- App layout: sidebar navigation, page header, global date-range + environment filter bar.
- Filter context shared across pages; drill-down from a chart into a filtered detail view.
- Global loading/error boundaries so a single failing widget doesn't blank the page.

Done when: an unauthenticated user is redirected to login, and filter state survives navigation between the two dashboards.

tasks.name: 4.6 Customer analytics dashboard page
tasks.details:
Assemble the customer-facing analytics surface.

Deliverables:
- KPI tiles: active customers, new customers, churn/retention rate, avg revenue per customer.
- Charts: customer growth over time, segment mix, cohort retention heatmap, geography breakdown.
- Customer table with search and drill-down to a single-customer timeline (tokenized ID, no PII exposed).
- Documented answers to the five questions the business asked this dashboard to answer.

Done when: a product stakeholder can answer "which segments are growing or shrinking" without analyst help.

tasks.name: 4.7 Application health & log analytics page
tasks.details:
Assemble the application health surface from the log pipeline metrics.

Deliverables:
- KPI tiles: error rate, p95 latency, request volume, error budget burn.
- Charts: error rate over time by service, latency percentile trends, top failing routes, traffic heatmap by hour.
- Funnel visualization page using the funnel metrics from 3.6.
- Drill-down: click a spike → filtered detail for that service/route/time window.

Done when: an on-call engineer can identify the worst-performing service and route for the last hour in under 30 seconds.

tasks.name: 4.8 Export, snapshot & saved views
tasks.details:
Let people get the data out and get back to a view.

Deliverables:
- CSV export of any table/chart's underlying data, respecting current filters and permissions.
- PDF/image snapshot of a dashboard page for sharing in reports.
- Saved views: named filter configurations per user.
- Export history/audit log noting who exported what.

Done when: an exported CSV row count matches the on-screen filtered result, and a saved view restores exactly.

tasks.name: 4.9 Performance budget & load optimization
tasks.details:
Make it fast, and prove it stays fast.

Deliverables:
- Published performance budget (e.g. LCP < 2.5s p95, time-to-first-chart < 1.5s, bundle size ceiling).
- Measurement in CI with a synthetic large dataset (not 10 rows — use realistic volume).
- Optimizations as needed: code splitting per route, chart data downsampling, virtualized tables, prefetch on hover.
- Regression guard: CI fails if the budget is exceeded.

Done when: both dashboard pages meet the budget on a large fixture dataset and CI enforces it.

tasks.name: 4.10 Accessibility audit & remediation
tasks.details:
Charts are routinely inaccessible — handle it deliberately rather than retrofitting.

Deliverables:
- Colorblind-safe palettes plus a non-color encoding (pattern/label) for categorical series.
- Keyboard navigation for filters, drill-down, and table interaction; visible focus states.
- Chart alternatives: data table fallback and descriptive summary text per chart for screen readers.
- Automated axe (or equivalent) checks in CI plus one manual screen-reader pass.

Done when: an automated audit reports no critical violations on core flows and a chart's data is reachable from the keyboard alone.

tasks.name: 4.11 Beta launch, telemetry & rollout plan
tasks.details:
Ship it to real users with a reversible rollout.

Deliverables:
- Pilot group access enabled (5-10 users from product + engineering).
- Instrumentation: page views, query latency, error rates, top failing widgets — dashboard usage is observable.
- Feedback channel + a triage list with owners for the first two weeks.
- Rollout plan: feature-flag gated expansion to wider audience, and a documented rollback path.
- Launch notes covering known limitations and data freshness expectations.

Done when: pilot users are active, telemetry is flowing, and rollback has been rehearsed (not just documented).

tasks.name: 3.5a Error rate & request volume aggregation
tasks.details:
One metric family, one job — keeps the schema and tests small.

Deliverables:
- Error-rate aggregation by service, route, and level (5xx rate, 4xx rate, explicit error-level count).
- Request-volume aggregation (total events, total requests, per-route split).
- Shared bucketing helper consumed by 3.5c.
- Tests against a hand-computed 1-day fixture for both metrics.

Done when: the 1-day fixture matches hand-computed error rate and volume exactly.

tasks.name: 3.5b Latency percentile aggregation & method validation
tasks.details:
The trickiest correctness problem in M3 — percentile accuracy under approximation.

Deliverables:
- Latency p50/p95/p99 by service and route.
- Explicit method decision documented (approximate quantile sketch vs exact sort), with the accuracy/storage trade-off written down.
- Validation test: computed p95 matches an independent exact calculation within a stated tolerance across at least three distributions (uniform, bimodal, heavy-tail).
- Handling of missing/null latency and non-numeric values, without silently skewing percentiles.

Done when: p95 stays within tolerance on all three distributions and null handling is covered by a test.

tasks.name: 3.5c Bucketing tiers & refresh scheduling
tasks.details:
Two granularity tiers and the scheduling around them.

Deliverables:
- 1-minute buckets for the recent window (recommend 48h) and 1-hour buckets for long history.
- Boundary correctness: events at minute/hour edges land in exactly one bucket, never two or zero.
- Scheduled refresh with a documented freshness SLA (e.g. no older than 5 minutes) and idempotent recompute of the current partial bucket.
- Data-volume estimate per tier so storage cost is known before it grows.

Done when: a bucket-boundary fixture produces exact counts per bucket, and a re-run of the partially-elapsed bucket corrects rather than double-counts.

tasks.name: 4.2a Line chart component
tasks.details:
Split out of 4.2 — the single most-used chart, worth building carefully.

Deliverables:
- Multi-series line chart with independent series toggling.
- Gap handling: missing data rendered as a gap, not interpolated as zero.
- Time-bucket-aware axis formatting (minutes/hours/days chosen from the range) and accessible tick labels.
- Tooltip showing all series values at the hovered timestamp.
- Responsive at three breakpoints; legend wraps rather than clipping.

Done when: a dataset with a deliberate 3-hour hole shows a visible gap, and the axis labels adapt correctly across 1h / 7d / 90d ranges.

tasks.name: 4.2b Bar & stacked-bar components
tasks.details:
Grouped and stacked modes share an axis and a data model, so build them together.

Deliverables:
- Grouped-bar mode (side-by-side categories) and stacked-bar mode (composition over time), switchable by prop.
- Handling of many categories: colour cycling or "Other" roll-up when series exceed the palette.
- Value labels on hover; accessible summary text for screen readers.
- Vertical and horizontal orientation.

Done when: the same dataset renders correctly in both modes, and 20 categories degrade gracefully instead of producing an unreadable chart.

tasks.name: 4.2c Sparkline & heatmap components
tasks.details:
Two small but fiddly components — the dense ones.

Deliverables:
- Sparkline: no axes, no labels, optional trend colour, fixed small footprint for KPI tiles; renders correctly for single-point and all-null series.
- Heatmap: consistent colour scale with a documented domain (fixed vs data-driven), weekday × hour layout, legend, and per-cell tooltip.
- Both honour the colorblind-safe palette and provide a data-table fallback (feeds 4.10).

Done when: sparkline survives degenerate series without crashing, and the heatmap's colour scale is stable across two different datasets (same bucket = same colour).
